LESSON: LANGUAGE USE 15.3.1 INTERJECTIONS OF DISPLEASURE

Grade: SNE  /  visual-impairment / Grade three
Subject: ENGLISH
Strand: Strand 15
Topic 15.3: Language Use 15.3.1 Interjections of Displeasure
Suggested lessons in curriculum: 2

SECTION 1: INTRODUCTION

This lesson covers Language Use 15.3.1 Interjections of Displeasure, part of Strand 15 in SNE  /  visual-impairment / Grade three ENGLISH.

Key inquiry question: How do you show that someone is not happy about something?

You will study the official KICD learning outcomes, classroom activities, values, and competencies for this topic. Use Kenyan examples from your county, school, and community throughout.

SECTION 2: LEARNING OUTCOMES

By the end of this topic, you should be able to:

Refer to the KICD curriculum reference at the end of this lesson for the full list of outcomes.

SECTION 3: KEY CONCEPTS AND EXPLANATION

SECTION 4: LEARNING ACTIVITIES

A. At school

Follow your teacher’s guidance for group work, discussion, and practice on this topic.

B. At home with your parent or guardian

1. Read this lesson on Language Use 15.3.1 Interjections of Displeasure together.
2. Discuss the key inquiry question and give examples from your area.
3. Write five sentences summarising what you learned.
4. Prepare for the revision quiz at the end of this topic.

SECTION 5: CORE COMPETENCIES, VALUES, AND PCIs

Core Competencies to be developed:
• Communication and collaboration: The learner’s ability to speak clearly and effectively as well as engage with others is enhanced as they work

together in pairs or groups as they use appropriate interjections to express displeasure.

• Learning to learn: The learner’s ability to develop relationships is improved they take part in playing a language game with peers.

Values:
• Unity: Cooperation is cultivated as the learner observes turn taking during language game activities with peers.

Link to

Pertinent and Contemporary Issues:
• Life-skills (Self-esteem): The learner acquires an elevated level of self-esteem as they learn how to express displeasure using the appropriate

interjections.
